findings.problem: TreeMap has public fields and can be constructed or mutated without new(). All scene constructors trust it. The safe Rust API can therefore pass invalid map bounds/sector dimensions to unsafe C.
findings.concrete_path: For example min_x=max_x=f32::MAX and sectors_x=sectors_z=2 can be passed to without_trees; a finite outside segment is clamped to f32::MAX in scan640 then get_terrain_3d_sector488 converts f32::MAX/2048 to int, outside its representable range. This is undefined C conversion, not a valid no-trees answer.
findings.correction: Make validated map invariants unforgeable or revalidate in every scene construction path, including absent-file/no-trees paths, before storing or FFI. Add public-API invalid literal/mutation coverage; preserve valid arithmetic.
findings.evidence_status: Source-confirmed safe public path; reviewer did not execute malformed native input.

findings.problem: The guard relies only on fegetenv/fesetenv and does not actually restore the complete caller SSE control/status state on the supported Windows build.
findings.concrete_path: All three actual Windows library replays first match default and Up numerical outputs, then fail restoration: before x87/SSE masks63/63, SSE RC2, x87 Up, flags0; after SSE RC3 and flags32 while x87 still Up. Windows unit contracts independently fail Nearest with RC0->3/flags0->33.
findings.correction: Explicitly preserve/restore relevant MXCSR and x87 environment across every entry outcome on the supported target, keeping original internal rounding and exception-mask refusal. Retain these REDs; verify caller modes and existing nonzero flags at request/done/refusal boundaries without weakening expectations.
findings.evidence_status: Actual Windows native failure101, retained controller/log hashes; numerical matches do not make restoration pass.

findings.problem: Public ScopedRounding contains only Vec<u64> and auto-implements Send/Sync although it captures and later restores calling-thread state.
findings.concrete_path: Safe Rust can create the guard on thread A, move it to B, and drop there. B receives A's saved FP state and A remains in the changed rounding mode; the stated lexical caller-state restoration is false.
findings.correction: Make the guard thread-bound (!Send/!Sync), or keep it private to tests with an equivalent enforced thread-local lifetime. Add a bounded type-level/compile control; do not require a new campaign.
findings.evidence_status: Source/type-system confirmed; no cross-thread native experiment executed.

findings.problem: Lua forest_geometry is read with sequence_values, which ends at the first nil. A sparse list or a hole silently drops later triangles instead of refusing malformed physical geometry.
findings.concrete_path: forest_geometry={[2]=triangle} becomes an empty Triangles mesh; a valid triangle1 followed by a hole silently omits its tail. The kernel then falls back to the quad path or consumes only a prefix.
findings.correction: Validate an actual dense ordered triangle list and reject holes/non-list keys rather than silently truncating. Add actual-host sparse/hole controls, with a valid dense geometry positive. Do not derive geometry or claim a native original-model witness.
findings.evidence_status: Source-confirmed and reproduced by actual unchanged d726 host in same-pass six-case protocol diagnostics; diagnostic process0 is not a passing negative guard.

findings.problem: New begin/terrain requests can fail parsing before TreeCollision is reached, leaving an old pending query live. Direct Rust begin clears open before validation, so the two interfaces differ.
findings.concrete_path: Valid begin returns NeedTerrain; a malformed replacement begin (e.g. old_position has only two numbers) is refused before holder.begin; a later terrain answer still advances the prior query. Nonfinite terrain parse refusal likewise leaves it pending. The synthetic test claims refused requests leave no query open but only tests unrelated completed states and manually abandons after the nonfinite reply.
findings.correction: Make the Lua boundary fail closed on malformed replacement/response requests, clearing/abandoning the pending query before accepting later continuation; cover pending->bad begin/terrain->later terrain refusal in the real host test. Preserve normal begin/request/answer ordering and arithmetic.
findings.evidence_status: Source-confirmed and reproduced by actual unchanged d726 host in same-pass six-case protocol diagnostics; diagnostic process0 is not a passing negative guard.

findings.problem: local negative_zero=0*-1 is folded by this Lua5.1 to positive zero, so the test does not supply its claimed -0 input.
findings.correction: Construct runtime negative zero, e.g. -1/math.huge, retain expected80000000 and tiny/subnormal checks. Do not change the reviewed exact numeric reader to satisfy a wrong input.
findings.evidence_status: Actual unchanged d726 host diagnostic: original construction reciprocal+inf/format0 exits1; only runtime construction replacement gives reciprocal-inf/format-0 and whole script0/TREE_COLLISION_HOST_OK.

findings.problem: The claim that lengths are checked before anything is allocated is overbroad: load() uses std::fs::read before from_bytes validates, and geometry_from allocates before header checks.
findings.correction: Qualify the precise checks before indexing/decoding, or add corresponding preallocation validation. Do not imply unbounded filesystem read is already bounded by these checks.
findings.evidence_status: Source/documentation correspondence only; no OOM/runtime defect asserted.

Query storage is private, size-queried and u64-aligned; no private campaign pointer/heap index/seed crosses this component.

Count/offset ranges are checked before tree indexing; zero-count offsets are not dereferenced.
